newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open flat to $5 lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open flat to $5 lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open unchanged to $5 a tonne lower on Monday, in line with losses overnight in London, traders said.
London cocoa futures were weaker early Monday in thin, rangebound dealings. LIFFE July cocoa was five stg lower at the midday break, at 990 stg. September was off eight stg, at 1,011 stg.

Friday, New York cocoa futures ended mixed, with speculative selling pressuring the nearby months. July futures fell $6 a tonne, to $1,413, having ranged between $1,408 and $1,425. September ended $4 weaker, at $1,455, while the outer months finished down $1 to up $1.
Technically, July support was pegged at toward the $1,404-$1,400 level, then $1,394. Resistance was seen at a chart gap from $1,432-1,441.

The latest CFTC Commitment of Traders report released Friday showed non-commercial long positions in the two weeks ended June 3 rose by 2,775 lots, to 16,369 lots. Non-commercial short positions fell by 733 lots, to 4,268 lots.
Commercial long positions in the two weeks fell by 3,485 lots, to 61,077 lots, while commercial short positions fell by 1,177 lots to 79,054 lots.
Non-reportable long positions rose by 459 lots to 16,058 lots and non-reportable short positions rose by 1,659 lots to 10,182 lots.

Traders said the report, which showed speculators (non-commercial plus non-reportable) net long nearly 18,000 lots in the latest tally, could weigh on sentiment. They noted, however, the data was through last Tuesday and many speculators had liquidated their positions since then.
